title: 2025-06-18-horizon-discovery-migration-openai-to-dedicated
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated sizing worksheet and pricing sheet
Customer to send example traffic profile and key evaluation prompts
Share SOC 2 + network architecture docs and KMS integration notes
action_items: Samir Patel: send Dedicated pricing + sizing (due 2025-06-20)
Lena Ortiz: schedule benchmark slot and request sample prompts (due 2025-06-19)
Rajiv Menon: provide traffic profile and PII/PHI constraints (due 2025-06-20)
Carlos Ruiz: confirm whether VPC peering or private link is preferred (due 2025-06-19)
summary: Discovery call focused on migration from OpenAI-hosted models to Redwood Dedicated. Customer is concerned about cost, throughput, and eval parity across models; wants a pilot to validate latency/quality and security posture (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Next steps: sizing/pricing, bench run, share security docs.
topics: deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript: 00:00 Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, with me is Lena our SE. Quick intros?
00:09 Rajiv: Rajiv here, CTO at Horizon AI. We run customer-facing recommender and search features, currently on OpenAI for generation and embeddings.
00:20 Emily: Emily, ML eng, I own model infra and evals. We're exploring moving away from OpenAI to reduce cost and get more control, maybe Dedicated or private.
00:33 Samir: Great. High level, are you leaning self-host (vLLM/TGI) or managed?

00:38 Rajiv: We considered self-host but vLLM setups got tricky — memory, KV cache tuning. Also TGI had some parity issues on longer contexts. So exploring Redwood Dedicated as an alternative for predictable throughput.
01:02 Lena: One thing we usually see — customers want eval parity with OpenAI outputs. Can you describe your acceptance criteria? Latency, token cost, hallucination rate?

01:15 Emily: Parity means similar top-k responses for our 1000 eval prompts and <= 10% regression on our quality metrics. Latency target 300ms per first token for short requests, 400-800ms for typical chat flows.
01:34 Carlos: And throughput — we have about 20 rps peak during business hours, with spikes up to 60 rps for short bursts. Cost sensitivity is high — current OpenAI spend is a big line item.
01:52 Samir: Good context. On Dedicated, we offer reserved GPU pools and can tailor batch sizes and quantization to fit cost/latency. Are you planning to pick a single model family or mix?
02:07 Rajiv: Mix. We use smaller models for assistant-like flows and larger ones for complex summarization. Also embeddings currently with OpenAI — we'd want embedding parity too.
02:20 Lena: Quick note — embedding API and vector store behavior can vary slightly, but we provide guidance on model selection and an eval harness to match embeddings semantics as much as possible.
02:32 Emily: Can Redwood run our evals? We want a bench comparing identical prompts across providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Redwood-hosted models (and local vLLM if we try it).
02:43 Samir: Absolutely, we usually run SE-led bench sessions. We'll need sample prompts and a traffic profile. Lena can schedule and run a parity benchmark on Dedicated nodes.
03:00 Rajiv: Security — must have SOC2, SSO, and KMS support for key material. Also we need VPC peering or private link for data egress constraints.
03:12 Lena: We support VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. KMS/HSM integrations are supported, and we can share SOC 2 and audit docs after the call.
03:24 Carlos: Are there differences in network patterns between Hosted and Dedicated? We need NAT rules, egress IPs, stuff the infra team handles.
03:34 Samir: Dedicated gives predictable egress and dedicated GPU pools; we can provide VPC details and IP ranges. For Private, you manage the network entirely.
04:00 Rajiv: Cost — how do you price Dedicated versus Hosted? We want to understand unit economics — tokens, inference vs pre-warm cost.

04:10 Samir: For Dedicated it's a reserved capacity model (monthly commit) plus per-token unit for some add-ons; Hosted is usage-based. We'll send a sizing worksheet and an example cost model based on your traffic profile.
04:27 Emily: Technical question on latency tuning — does Redwood support KV cache reuse and streaming? Our main issue on vLLM was KV cache invalidation across shards.
04:38 Lena: Yes, runtime supports KV cache management, continuous batching, and streaming responses. For shard-level cache we have strategies to keep warm caches for hot prefixes.
04:50 Rajiv: Any gotchas with model flavors — say we want to use OpenAI-compatible endpoint semantics — will prompts and stop tokens behave identically?
05:01 Samir: We aim compatibility but there's subtle differences across model implementations. That's why the eval parity run is important; small prompt engineering tweaks usually bring parity.
05:15 Emily: We also run reranking in-house — do you support hybrid architectures where embeddings live in our vector DB but generation happens in Redwood?
05:23 Lena: Yes, many customers do that. We support embeddings and generation as separate routes; we can keep embeddings in your DB and generation in Dedicated.
05:34 Rajiv: On the self-host vs Dedicated decision — our infra team likes the control of self-host but we don't want to own all the reliability work. How do your SLAs compare?
05:45 Samir: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Private is more like a licensed deployment where you manage infra but we support the control plane.
06:00 Carlos: Important — can we get logs/audit trails for token-level usage? Compliance needs per-request audit logs retained for 90 days.
06:09 Lena: Yes we provide observability in the Console with per-token breakdowns, traces, and exportable audit logs; retention is configurable as an add-on.
06:22 Rajiv: Bench pieces — would you recommend quantization for our workloads? We worry about quality regressions.
06:30 Samir: We'll run recommended quantization profiles per-model and measure quality impact in the eval. Redwood Optimize recommends profiles by workload.
06:42 Emily: About model repo — do you host curated open models and do you verify performance profiles?
06:48 Lena: Yes, model catalog with verified performance profiles, and we help pick nearest-compatible variants for fallbacks.
07:00 Rajiv: For demos we want to test a few workflows: short chat, long summarization (4k-8k), and embedding similarity. Can you simulate our load?
07:10 Samir: Yes, provide sample prompts and we can replay traffic shape. We'll include warm-up and burst tests to validate tail latency.
07:22 Emily: There are some internal constraints — some requests contain PII and we must ensure data residency (EU region) and KMS key separation.
07:33 Lena: We have region pinning and KMS per-tenant options on Dedicated and Private deployments.
07:45 Carlos: Integrations — we use Okta SAML and have RBAC needs. Does Redwood support SCIM or SAML SSO?
07:52 Samir: Yes SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning are supported; we'll send a security checklist after the call.
08:05 Rajiv: Competitors — we've seen Anthropic and Azure's OpenAI Service in procurement. How do you compare on price/perf?
08:15 Samir: Roughly, Dedicated can beat Azure on unit economics if you commit and leverage batching and quantization. We also provide observable metrics and fallbacks which customers find valuable.

08:32 Emily: A few transcription notes from our side — sometimes vLLM's output distribution is slightly different which affects our reranker. We'd want to see top-k distributions when you run the bench.
08:44 Lena: We can export logits distribution or n-best lists as part of the eval to debug reranker sensitivity.
09:00 Rajiv: Are there constraints on model length / KV cache size per GPU? For long summarization we need good KV handling up to 16k.
09:12 Lena: There are hardware limits but we can choose model sharding or sequence packing strategies; we'll propose configurations after we see your workload.
09:28 Samir: Quick interruption — sorry, any regulatory constraints, e.g., HIPAA?
09:34 Rajiv: Not full HIPAA but some clients have PHI in minimal flows so encryption at rest and in transit plus audit is mandatory.
09:44 Lena: We'll include encryption details and KMS flow in the security pack.
10:00 Emily: Can we get a pilot timeline? We want to run a 2-week parity pilot then ramp if results are good.
10:07 Samir: Typical pilot is 1-2 weeks of bench + 2-4 weeks of live shadow traffic. For Dedicated we can do a short bench on host-shared infra then move to reserved nodes for more realistic numbers.
10:22 Carlos: Any required infra changes on our side for Dedicated?
10:27 Lena: Mostly networking: VPC peering or private link, some firewall rules for egress. We'll give exact IP ranges and runbook.
10:38 Rajiv: About model compatibility — we use some OpenAI-specific attributes like logprobs and function calling; how mature is Redwood's function call compatibility?
10:51 Samir: We support function/tool calling and structured outputs. There can be small differences in serialization; part of the parity bench is to validate function call semantics.
11:05 Emily: There will be occasional transcription errors in our notes; just flagging that when we compare runs we may need to align tokenization differences.
11:12 Lena: Good point — we'll normalize tokenization and share tokenization diffs in the bench report.
11:28 Samir: Any blockers for starting the pilot?
11:32 Rajiv: Need internal buy-in on budget and legal sign-off; procurement timeline maybe 3-4 weeks. But we can start the bench without full procurement.
11:42 Samir: Perfect. We'll send the pricing and SOC docs, Lena will send a bench request and calendar invite.
11:50 Carlos: One small question — for embeddings do you support batch API with higher throughput?
11:58 Lena: Yes, batching for embeddings is supported and we can tune batch sizes for throughput/latency tradeoffs.
12:10 Rajiv: If the pilot shows regression, what's the rollback/fallback strategy?
12:18 Samir: We have smart routing and fallback to alternative model variants or hosted endpoints; can route by policy to keep live traffic safe.
12:30 Emily: About the eval harness, we want Git-friendly reports so our SREs can replay any failing prompt. Can you provide artifacts?
12:39 Lena: We'll provide bench results, logs, n-best lists, and a diff report you can check into your repo.
12:50 Rajiv: Ok that sounds good. Any additional questions from your side?
12:56 Samir: No, just to confirm next steps — send pricing, security docs, bench schedule. Anything else?
13:04 Emily: Also include required network config and expected IP ranges so infra can review.
13:12 Samir: Will do. Thanks all, we'll follow up with the action items.
13:18 Rajiv: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
13:22 [call ends]
